description: What gauge wire you need for a circuit: copper or aluminum size from the NEC ampacity table at the right temperature column, with the 125% continuous-load rule, the small-conductor breaker limits and an optional voltage-drop check for long runs. Formula: Design amps = load × 1.25 if continuous. Size = smallest AWG whose ampacity in the 60 °C (or 75 °C) column, capped by 240.4(D) for 14/12/10 AWG, is at least the design amps. Voltage drop % = 2 × K × I × L ÷ cmil ÷ V × 100 (√3 for three phase; K = 12.9 copper, 21.2 aluminum); step up until within the limit.

continuous.description: Continuous load (3 hours or more)?; default 1; one of 1 = Yes (size at 125%), 0 = No

one_way_ft.description: One-way length (0 = skip voltage drop) (ft); default 100

phase.description: Phase; default 1; one of 1 = Single phase, 3 = Three phase

terminal_c.description: Breaker/terminal rating; default 60; one of 60 = 60 °C (default for 100 A or less), 75 = 75 °C (listed equipment, or over 100 A)

name: calc_wire_size
title: Wire Size Calculator (Ampacity, 125% Rule and Voltage Drop)
